newsitem.title: INDIA: India MRPL receives dues from government.
newsitem.headline: India MRPL receives dues from government.

text.p: Indian refiner Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) said it started receiving payments under the government's administered pricing mechanism for petroleum products.
The payments are made from the oil pool account managed by the oil coordination committee of the ministry of petroleum and natural gas.
During the six months ended September 30, 1996, the company operated at an average capacity utilisation of 72.47 percent, processing 1.08 million tonnes of crude oil, it said.
The company achieved a turnover of 3.94 billion rupees, and a net profit of 174.3 million rupees for the six months ended September 30, 1996, the firm said after a Friday board meeting.
MRPL started commercial production at the southern port town of Mangalore on March 25, 1996.

The company has received all approvals for expanding the processing capacity to 9.0 million tonnes from 3.0 million tonnes. "The physical work on expansion project in Mangalore is expected to start shortly," it said.
